web.description:
Jessica Stanley

# Warhol's Marilyn Sells for $195 Million
**NEW YORK** – Monday, May 9, 2022 Christie’s Spring Marquee Week of sales began with the momentous sale of **_Shot Sage Blue Marilyn_** by **Andy Warhol**, selling for $195 million, establishing it as the most expensive 20th century artwork to sell at auction. The painting was the final lot of Christie’s single-owner evening sale [The Collection of Thomas and Doris Ammann](https://www.christies.com/auction/the-collection-of-thomas-and-doris-ammann-evening-sale-21508-nyr), which featured 36 lots and totaled $317.8 Million.

**Ann Craven**’s _I Wasn’t Sorry, 2003_ achieved eight times the previous record, fetching $680,400, with competition from 15 bidders. The other records were: **Mike** **Bidlo** (three times the previous record), **Mary Heilmann, Martin Disler,** and **Ross Bleckner**. After Warhol’s Marilyn, the top lots were Cy Twombly’s _Untitled_, which achieved $21 million; Robert Ryman’s _Untitled_, which sold for $20.1 million; and Cy Twombly’s _Venere Sopra Gaeta_, at $16.9 million.

web.title: Most expensive 20th-century painting sold at auction
web.description:
The most expensive painting from the 20th century sold at auction is _Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer_ (1914–16) by Austrian artist Gustav Klimt, which achieved $236,400,000 (£179.6 m; €203.8 m) – including premium/fees – at Sotheby’s in New York City, USA, on 18 November 2025.

Prior to that, the record stood with Pablo Picasso’s _The Women of Algiers (Version “O”)_ (1955), which sold for $179,365,000 (£116 m; €160 m), also at Christie’s in New York, on 11 May 2015.

David Geffen Foundation sold _Interchanged_ to billionaire hedge-fund manager Kenneth Griffin. At the same sale, Griffin bought another significant Abstract Expressionist work: Jackson Pollock’s _Number 17A_ (1948).

Auction records make for great headlines, like [Tuesday’s banner sale](https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/gustav-klimt-portrait-of-elisabeth-lederer-auction-record-1234762083/) of Gustav Klimt’s _Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer_ (1914–16), which topped $236.4 million at Sotheby’s.

## Pablo Picasso, _Woman with a Watch_, 1932
It was acquired by Landau in 1968 from Pace Gallery, which had purchased it from Switzerland’s Galerie Beyeler two years earlier.

In 2010, _Nude, Green Leaves and Bust_—also painted in 1932—broke records at $106.5 million.

## Alberto Giacometti, _Pointing Man_, 1947
The life-size bronze, standing at more than five and a half feet tall, was sold by real estate magnate Sheldon Solow, surpassing Giacometti’s previous auction record of $104.3 million, which was set at Sotheby’s London five years earlier by _Walking Man I_ (1960).

## Francis Bacon, _Three Studies of Lucian Freud_, 1969
Francis Bacon’s _Three Studies of Lucian Freud_ (1969) briefly became the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction when it sold for [$142.4 million at Christie’s New York in November 2013.](https://www.artnews.com/art-in-america/features/christies-achieves-record-6914-million-as-bacon-becomes-most-expensive-auction-trophy-59589/) The triptych surpassed the previous record, held by Edvard Munch’s pastel _The Scream_, which sold for $119.9 million at Sotheby’s in 2012 (and which also appears on this list, above).

## Pablo Picasso, _Women of Algiers (Version ‘O’)_, 1955
Pylkkänen, serving as auctioneer, declared “Still many people in the game” as bidding climbed past $140 million.

While Christie’s maintained confidentiality regarding the winning bidder, reports later suggested that the buyer was former Qatari Prime Minister [Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani](https://www.artnews.com/list/art-news/artists/pablo-picasso-highest-auction-records-1234594915/).

## Jackson Pollock, _Number 7A, 1948_, 1948
Alfred Taubman owned the painting, selling it to publishing magnate S.

## Andy Warhol, _Shot Sage Blue Marilyn_, 1964
**Sold for $195 million at Christie’s New York in May 2022**

Andy Warhol’s _Shot Sage Blue Marilyn_, one of the most iconic images in modern art, became the most expensive 20th-century artwork ever sold at auction when it fetched $195 million at Christie’s New York in 2022.

Art dealer Larry Gagosian, bidding in person, ultimately secured the painting with a hammer price of $170 million, well below its $200 million estimate.

## Gustav Klimt’s _Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer_, 1914–16
The full-length portrait, one of only two named Klimt commissions in private hands, was the undisputed centerpiece of the sale of the Leonard A.

Bidding opened at $130 million and unfolded over 20 tense minutes, narrowing to two phone bidders represented by Sotheby’s specialists David Galperin and Julian Dawes. Dawes’s bidder ultimately won with a hammer price of $205 million, prompting applause in the salesroom and marking the most expensive lot ever handled by Sotheby’s.

# The 10 Most Expensive Artworks Ever Sold
## Salvator Mundi by Leonardo da Vinci – $450 Million
Acquired by an anonymous buyer, later revealed to be acting on behalf of Saudi Prince Bader bin Abdullah bin Mohammed bin Farhan Al Saud.

## The Card Players by Paul Cézanne – $250 Million
This particular rendition, exuding an air of serene concentration, was acquired in 2011 by the royal family of Qatar for $250 million.

## Number 17A by Jackson Pollock – $200 Million
Acquired by Kenneth C.

## Shot Sage Blue Marilyn by Andy Warhol – $195 Million
Andy Warhol’s Shot Sage Blue Marilyn shattered records at a 2022 Christie’s auction, selling for just over $195 million to art dealer Larry Gagosian.
